                    <div class="text"><p> </p>
<p><strong>The EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Quantum Informatics (QI CDT) invites applications for up to 16 fully funded four-year PhD studentships in Quantum Informatics with Integrated Study for September 2027 entry.</strong></p>
<p>Quantum computing provides unprecedented means to overcome bottlenecks of complex problems. The greatest impediment to realising the potential of quantum computing is the lack of people power. End-to-end solutions take years to develop and require skills outside traditional quantum engineering and physics. They require Quantum Informatics: enabling the use of quantum technology in ways that are interoperable and impactful.</p>
<p>The QI CDT, a consortium of five institutions (University of Edinburgh, Heriot-Watt University, University College London, Oxford University, and University of Strathclyde), is offering up to 16 fully funded four-year PhDs in Quantum Informatics to train a new generation of students in the interaction of quantum hardware, software, and applications.</p>
<p>A cohort-based 4-year PHD programme with integrated study offers comprehensive, interdisciplinary training that bridges computer science, mathematics, physics, and engineering. It equips students to tackle complex quantum challenges while considering their commercial and societal impacts.</p>
<p>These PhDs will begin in September 2027, and the deadline to apply is <strong>7<sup>th</sup> January 2027</strong>.</p>
<p> </p>
<p><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>Benefits of Joining the Programme</strong></span></p>
<ul>
<li>A unique first-year training programme (taught year), including courses and cohort-building events, providing the skills and knowledge required for a quantum PhD</li>
<li>Opportunities to enhance research and professional skills through leadership programmes, outreach events, spring schools, residential symposia, and enhanced training</li>
<li>A three-year research project supported by a research training support grant, and further cohort-building and training events</li>
<li>Residential programme at the National Quantum Computing Centre</li>
<li>70+ academic supervisors from across our five partner institutions</li>
<li>30+ global industry partners offering close collaboration on projects, internships, and placements</li>
<li>Generous support for entrepreneurship and start-up development</li>
<li>Diverse future career paths in Research & Academia; Industry & Technology; Consulting & Strategy; Data Science & Cryptography; Entrepreneurship & Start-ups</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<p><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>Funding and Eligibility</strong></span></p>
<p>Funding covers tuition fees and a stipend for 4 years, and an individual budget for travel and research costs. Both UK and international students are eligible for the funding.</p>
<p>Applicants must have or expect to obtain the equivalent of a 1st or 2:1 degree in any subject relevant to the CDT, including, but not limited to, computing science, engineering, mathematics, and physics.</p>
<p><strong> </strong></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>Student Support </strong></span></p>
<p>We seek to foster an inclusive and accessible environment where everybody feels supported and respected. The CDT programme offers tailored support and flexible working patterns to meet individual student needs. Studies can be undertaken on a part-time basis to accommodate students wishing to combine their studies with work or personal responsibilities. All CDT studentships are fully funded and have provisions for sick pay, parental leave, and disabled students’ support. We also provide individual coaching sessions to students from underrepresented groups to support their PhD journey and post-PhD career choices.</p>
<p> </p>
<p><span style="font-size: 14pt;"><strong>How to Apply</strong></span></p>
<p>Applications must be submitted through the University of Edinburgh’s (our lead institution) online application system, where you will be required to submit <strong>a CV, a Statement of Intent, two references, and your academic certificate(s) and transcript(s). </strong>For full details, please visit our website <a href="https://study.ed.ac.uk/programmes/postgraduate-research/1130-centre-for-doctoral-training-in-quantum-informatics?utm_source=STEMWomen&utm_medium=Listing&utm_campaign=UoE-Inf-CDTQuantInf-26">here</a>.</p>
<p>For any enquiries, please contact the CDT Team at <a href="mailto:info@quantuminformatics-cdt.ac.uk">info@quantuminformatics-cdt.ac.uk</a>.</p>
